explanation: With no air to slow the feather, both fell at the same rate, as Galileo had argued. Commander David Scott did the test on Apollo 15, live on television.

claims.text: When David Scott dropped a hammer and a feather together on the Moon in 1971, they hit the ground at the same time.
On the Moon the hammer did not land before the feather, and the feather did not float away.
Without air resistance, objects fall at the same rate whatever their mass.
Galileo argued that bodies of different weight would fall at the same rate apart from air resistance.
David Scott, commander of Apollo 15, did the hammer and feather drop on the Moon, shown live on television.
